nv_wobble.blurb: Wobble is a small cluster of eleven boulder problems up the wash in Mystery Canyon, in Red Rock's Willow Spring zone. The sandstone blocs run from easy-to-moderate problems around V2 and V3 up through a handful of V4 and V5 lines, then a group of hard problems near V8 and one harder still. Boulders are modest in height, so pads matter more than spotters on the taller lines. It is a short walk beyond the larger Sad Robot boulder at the canyon mouth, which makes it a good add-on for a strong boulderer rather than a destination for beginners. Expect quiet conditions and fragile rock that is best left alone when damp.

nv_upper_keystone_canyon.blurb: Upper Keystone Canyon is a boulder field on the west side of Reno, reached on foot from the Keystone Canyon trailhead by following the trail, then a dirt road that climbs the hillside past a first field of blocks. Eleven problems are recorded, almost all in the easy range from V0 to V2, with just a couple of harder lines up to roughly V5. The rock is pocketed and featured but can be loose in places, so test holds and bring more than one pad with a spotter. It suits a casual evening session close to town rather than a full-day trip.

nv_amerradets.blurb: Amerradets is a steep limestone wall in the remote Mormon Mountains of southern Nevada, with eleven sport routes. Climbs are overhanging and short, roughly 45 to 75 feet, and the grades are firmly hard: one in the low 5.11s, a handful of 5.12s and the rest 5.13. The wall faces north and sits in shade all day, which makes it a spring, fall or mild-winter objective. The walk-in takes about half an hour, passing the neighbouring Brevity Wall and heading for a flat-topped fin of rock. The range is quiet and undeveloped, so expect solitude and a long dirt-road drive.

nv_meetup_wall.blurb: Meetup Wall is a bolted sandstone face tucked behind the busier crags of the Second Pullout in Calico Hills, Red Rock. Most of its eleven climbs are sport routes with lower-off anchors, plus one crack that needs a trad rack. Grades stay friendly, from about 5.6 to 5.10, with the bulk in the 5.7 to 5.9 range, so it works well for newer leaders and groups. The routes face southwest. Plan on a long first walk, up to an hour, past the Sweet Pain area and up a gully; top ropes can be rigged from the anchors on the easier lines.

nv_mud_spring_wing.blurb: Mud Spring Wing is a run of east- and south-facing sandstone walls at the mouth of Mud Spring Canyon, on the southeast shoulder of Black Velvet Peak in Red Rock. Eleven routes are recorded, mostly traditional with a few bolted lines, spanning 5.7 up to the low 5.12s with a solid cluster at 5.11. The approach is a steep, cairned slog that takes the better part of an hour, and the canyon stays uncrowded with a remote feel. It suits competent parties who are comfortable with route-finding and a full rack.
nv_mud_spring_wing.parking_note: Leave the car in the lot used for Black Velvet Canyon and walk from there.

nv_chocolate_rocks.blurb: Chocolate Rocks are the southernmost cliffs in Red Rock, reached straight from the Blue Diamond Highway. All eleven recorded climbs are traditional, mostly short crack and corner lines from about 5.6 to 5.10, with the heaviest concentration around 5.7 to 5.8. The brown, varnished bands face south and east, so they catch plenty of sun and suit cooler days. The approach drops into a wash and scrambles up through pale and pink bands on a cairned path. Few parties come here, so the sandstone stays quiet.
